body.statement: Suppose \(q_x>0\) for both \(x\in B\).  The weak legal parameterization by one unconditional law \(\mu\), initial kernel \(h\), and unrestricted feedback kernel \(g\) is exactly equivalent, at the level of the joint law \(P\) and the unconditional APE \(\Delta\), to the Bonhomme--Dano--Graham \(T=2\) unrestricted-feedback parameterization conditional on \(X_1=x\): normalization of the finite measure \(h_xd\mu\) by \(q_x\) gives the conditional heterogeneity law, and the reverse map takes the \(q_x\)-weighted mixture of the two conditional laws and recovers \(h_x\) by a Radon--Nikodym derivative.  This is an unrestricted-measure correspondence on the continuous state space \((0,\infty)\), so atomic, absolutely continuous, and mixed laws are permitted.  The strict class \(\mathcal M_+(c)\) is an additional subclass of the weak correspondence.  The equivalence does not establish that every atomic or mixed representation can be replaced by a Lebesgue-density representation, and hence does not establish exact correspondence with a separately imposed Lebesgue-density specialization.
body.proof_tex:
Let \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm w}(c)\) generate \(P\).  Summing its sequential path law over \(y,z,w\), and using in order \(\sum_w p_z(w,u)=1\), \(\sum_zg_{xy}(z,u)=1\), and \(\sum_yp_x(y,u)=1\), gives
\[
 q_x=\sum_{y,z,w}P(x,y,z,w)=\int h_x(u)\,d\mu(u). \tag{1}
\]
Because \(q_x>0\), define for every Borel set \(E\subset(0,\infty)\)
\[
 \pi_x(E)=q_x^{-1}\int_E h_x(u)\,d\mu(u). \tag{2}
\]
Equation (1) makes \(\pi_x\) a probability measure.  The path and APE equations become
\[
 P(x,y,z,w)
 =q_x\int p_x(y,u)g_{xy}(z,u)p_z(w,u)\,d\pi_x(u), \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \Delta
 =\sum_{x\in B}q_x\int
 \frac{(c-1)u}{(1+u)(1+cu)}\,d\pi_x(u), \tag{4}
\]
because \(\sum_xh_x=1\) \(\mu\)-almost everywhere.  These are the conditional-on-\(X_1\) measure equations, with the same unrestricted feedback kernel, identified in \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}continuous\text{-}feedback\text{-}program}\).

Conversely, let \(q_0,q_1>0\) sum to one, let \(\pi_0,\pi_1\) be probability measures on \((0,\infty)\), and let \(g\) be a normalized nonnegative feedback kernel in the conditional parameterization.  Define
\[
 \mu=\sum_{x\in B}q_x\pi_x. \tag{5}
\]
This is a probability measure, and each finite measure \(q_x\pi_x\) is dominated by \(\mu\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}radon\text{-}nikodym\text{-}finite\text{-}family}\), choose measurable versions
\[
 h_x=\frac{d(q_x\pi_x)}{d\mu},
 \qquad h_x\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_{x\in B}h_x=1
 \quad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}. \tag{6}
\]
Substitution of \(h_xd\mu=q_xd\pi_x\) into the sequential legal-model formulas turns (3)--(4) back into the unconditional path and APE equations.  Thus (2) and (5)--(6) are inverse at the level of all observable cells and the target, proving the weak unrestricted-measure correspondence.

Every element of \(\mathcal M_+(c)\) satisfies all weak restrictions by \(\mathrm{def{:}strict\text{-}legal\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}weak\text{-}legal\text{-}class}\), so the strict model is an additional subclass; no second comparison with the full weak Bonhomme--Dano--Graham fiber follows.  Finally, neither direction changes the measure class: (2) and (5) preserve atoms and singular components.  The finite Stieltjes converse in \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone\text{-}all\text{-}laws}\) may in particular return atomic laws.  Without an additional theorem replacing every such solution by one absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure while preserving all equations and restrictions, the argument cannot imply equality with a Lebesgue-density specialization.  This proves exactly the stated scope and no more.
